source_text: Quaeritur cur Canticum Canticorum appelletur. Sicut Sancta Sanctorum praecellunt sanctis, sic hoc canticum ceteris canticis. Praecesserunt cantica Moysi, Debborae, David, Isaiae et alia; ad ultimum ponitur hoc, ad quod per gradus canticorum anima proficiens pervenit. Quidam etiam cantica graduum et alia psalmorum cantica in numerum praecedentium adsciscunt, ut ostendant quam magnificis gressibus sponsa ad thalamum sponsi perveniat.
pass_a_gloss: It-is-asked why Song of-Songs it-is-called. As Holy of-Holies surpass holies, so this song other songs. There-preceded songs of-Moses, of-Deborah, of-David, of-Isaiah...
pass_b_english: It is asked why it is called the Song of Songs. As the Holy of Holies surpasses holy things, so this song surpasses other songs. Songs of Moses, Deborah, David, Isaiah and others came before; this is placed last, to which the advancing soul arrives by steps of songs. Some also bring the songs of ascents and other songs of the Psalms into the number of those that precede, to show by how magnificent steps the Bride comes to the Bridegroom’s chamber.
